**How the state is derived.** A requirement is <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> when a test
on `main` cites its id in a comment (the integration tests under `crates/*/tests` and the
`#[cfg(test)]` modules under `crates/*/src`, matched as a whole token; the files are linked in the
*evidence* column; a comment that says the feature is reserved, not implemented, refused as R2 or
R3, or of a later release cites the id without implementing it, and such a file is noted, not counted).
An id cited plainly in some test files and as a reserved feature in others is
<span class="state-part">implemented in part</span>, with both lists, counted on its own and not as implemented. It or when the Epic [#1](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/1) checklist assigns it to an issue that is
closed; the row says which of the two applies, and when only one does, what the other says.
A requirement is <span class="state-part">in progress</span> when its issue is open and has a branch on GitHub or an
open pull request, and <span class="state-no">planned</span> otherwise, with its release tag. The
SRS's own status field, in the *SRS status* column, changes only when a release revises the
document, so it is *Draft* for every requirement today (by SRS status: Draft 187)
and is not what the [progress](progress.html) page counts: that page reads the *state* column of each
component table below, implemented as done, implemented in part and in progress as progress, planned as later. The tracker
state is read live from GitHub
(`data/progress-snapshot.json`, fetched 2026-11-13 01:54 UTC); the
[issues](issues.html) page computes its *SRS requirements implemented* headline from the same code.

| RI-KC-001 | Kernels SHALL be written as Rust generators: functions taking a parameter struct (dtypes, tiles, layouts, pipeline depth, fused epilogue) and emitting Kernel IR through a builder; no kernel SHALL exist as MLIR text, HIP, OpenCL or assembly source except through a generator (RI-KC-009). *Rationale: ADR-005; the generator is the unit the autotuner explores.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> — by tests only; the Epic assigns it to open #9 | Draft | tests: [`rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs); Epic: open [#9](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/9) (not started) |
| RI-KC-002 | The Kernel IR SHALL be an MLIR dialect at tile level with explicit layouts: tiles, memory spaces (global, shared, register), barriers, a matrix-multiply op, masked loads and stores, reductions, structured control flow; thread identity SHALL NOT appear. *Rationale: A tile IR retargets to SIMT, vector and mesh devices; a thread IR does not.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> — by tests and epic | Draft | tests: [`rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs), [`rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs), [`rustinfer-kc/tests/mlir_link.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/mlir_link.rs); Epic: closed [#7](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/7) |

| id | text | priority | release | state | SRS status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-SCH-001 | New requests SHALL be admitted between iterations into one padding-free iteration with prefill requests first (in-flight batching). | Critical | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-002 | Decode tokens SHALL be scheduled before prefill tokens within `max_batch_size` and `max_num_tokens`. | Critical | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-003 | Policies `max_utilization`, `guaranteed_no_evict` and `static_batch` SHALL be selectable; the default from R2 SHALL be `max_utilization` with chunked prefill on. *Rationale: The first-class workload.* | High | R1 (static_batch); R2 (the rest) | <span class="state-no">planned R1</span> | Draft | Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |

| RI-SCH-005 | The overlap scheduler SHALL run the host work of iteration n during the device work of iteration n+1, on by default, disable-able per executor. | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-006 | Under `max_utilization`, when KV blocks run out the lowest-priority, most-recently-admitted decode request SHALL be paused and later resumed from its retained or recomputed prefix. | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-007 | Requests SHALL carry a priority (default 0) and optional deadline; admission SHALL order by priority then arrival; an expired request SHALL fail. | Medium | R3 | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-008 | LoRA requests SHALL batch with base requests up to `max_loras` adapters per iteration. | High | R3 | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-009 | Iteration statistics SHALL record prefill and decode counts, scheduled tokens, KV blocks used and free, reuse hits, iteration latency and paused requests. | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-SCH-010 | The scheduler state SHALL be a single uniform token-level model for prefill, chunked prefill, decode, reuse and speculation (no separate queues per phase). *Rationale: vLLM V1's lesson: features compose when the scheduler is uniform.* | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |

## 3.2.13 KV cache

| id | text | priority | release | state | SRS status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-KVC-001 | The cache SHALL be a pool of fixed-size token blocks (power of two, default 32, recorded in the Plan) with one page size for all KV groups and, per sequence, one block table per group (RI-MIR-010); the tables SHALL live on the device (RI-RT-010). | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> — by tests only; the Epic assigns it to open #13 | Draft | tests: [`rustinfer-core/tests/constants.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-core/tests/constants.rs); Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |
| RI-KVC-002 | Allocation and release SHALL be O(1) from one pre-allocated pool with an LRU free list; no per-block heap allocation at run time. *Rationale: vLLM V1's block pool; prefix reuse must cost nothing at a 0 percent hit rate.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-no">planned R1</span> | Draft | Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |

| RI-KVC-004 | A sequence longer than the profile's `max_seq_len` SHALL be refused at admission. | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-no">planned R1</span> | Draft | Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |
| RI-KVC-005 | Filled blocks SHALL be indexed in a radix tree keyed by (token prefix, KV group, LoRA id, multimodal item hashes, optional per-request `cache_salt`); a new request SHALL reuse matching blocks and skip their computation and SHALL NOT match a block whose key differs in any component; reuse SHALL be on by default; hits and misses SHALL be counted. *Rationale: SGLang's RadixAttention; agent traffic served well by default.* | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-006 | Eviction SHALL be prioritised LRU with per-block priority (0 to 100, default 35) and optional retention windows; only unreferenced leaf blocks are evictable. | Medium | R3 | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-007 | Evicted blocks MAY be offloaded to host DRAM, CXL memory or NVMe tiers under the planner's KV policy and restored on reuse. | Medium | R3 (DRAM, NVMe); R4 (CXL, remote) | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-008 | FP8 and INT8 cache storage with per-block scales SHALL be supported where the catalog's attention kernels read them. | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | Draft | — |
